items.followUp: Define oscillatory motion and give one example.

rubric.why: Vibratory motion is a repeated to-and-fro motion about a mean position.
rubric.description: Defines the to-and-fro motion about a mean position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both the to-and-fro nature and that the motion is about the mean position.

rubric.why: A suitable example completes the definition.
rubric.description: Gives an example of vibratory motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example, such as the vibrating prongs of a tuning fork.

modelAnswer: Vibratory motion is the repeated to-and-fro motion of a body about its mean position.
Example: The prongs of a tuning fork vibrate.

items.followUp: Describe one experiment that demonstrates atmospheric pressure.

rubric.why: The weight of the air gives rise to atmospheric pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that air has weight or that the weight of air gives rise to pressure.

rubric.why: A relevant example demonstrates the effect of atmospheric pressure.
rubric.description: Gives an example of atmospheric pressure in action.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example, such as atmospheric pressure crushing a heated can as it cools.

modelAnswer: The atmosphere exerts pressure because air has weight.
For example, when a heated tin can containing a little water is cooled, atmospheric pressure can crush it.

items.followUp: How does torque change if the applied force is doubled while the moment arm stays constant?

rubric.why: Torque is the product of the force and its perpendicular moment arm.
rubric.description: States the relation between torque, force and moment arm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the relation torque = force × moment arm.

rubric.why: At constant force, doubling the moment arm doubles the torque.
rubric.description: States the effect of doubling the moment arm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the torque doubles, assuming the force remains constant.

modelAnswer: If the force remains constant and the moment arm is doubled, the torque doubles.
